text.p: These are the leading stories in Skopje press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonia mulls construction of oil pipeline between Skopje and Thesaloniki. The issue will be discussed at the conference on the Balkan energy cooperation in Thesaloniki next Thursday.
- The government has bought about 90 percent of the 18,900 tonnes of 1996 tobacco production.
- Newly elected mayors in 124 Macedonian municipalities are without basic conditions for work.
- Number of passangers departing from Skopje and Ohrid, two Macedonian airports, in 1996 fell to 528,458 from 624,361 departures in 1995.
- The association of foreign currency depositors whose savings have been frozen in Macedonian banks demand the monthly limit withdrawals to be increased to 300 German marks from 100 marks.
- Every third applicant for the American and German visas is rejected.
